problem:
A particle of mass $3\,\text{kg}$ is attached to a massless spring. The spring constant associated with the spring is $k=15\,{\text{kg/s}}^{2}.$  The particle is also subject to the resistive force that's proportional to the particle's velocity with a damping coefficient $c=12\,\text{kg/s},$ and an external force given by $F(t)=6{e}^{4t}\,\text{N}.$   

The position of the particle is $y(t)$ (measured in meters), and $t>0$ is the time in seconds.  If the particle moves with forced harmonic motion, what is the governing equation?
worked_solution:
The general equation of forced harmonic motion with damping is

$$
m{y}^{″}=-c{y}^{′}-ky+F(t).
$$

Substituting our values for $m,$ $k,$ $c$ and $F(t)$ gives

$$
3{y}^{″}=-12{y}^{′}-15y+6{e}^{4t}.
$$

Simplifying and rearranging the above equation, we get

$$
{y}^{″}+4{y}^{′}+5y=2{e}^{4t}.
$$
